findings.summary: The new os.Chmod changes the mode of existing directories (e.g. "."), which can strip group/other access or fail if the process doesn't own it; MkdirAll never did this.

The perm argument is applied to the directory rather than the file, so a file-style mode like 0o644 makes the directory untraversable and os.Create fails for non-root users; the doc comment doesn't explain this.

TestSaveUploadedFileWithPermission saves to "permission_test", so it checks the package directory's mode (changed by the new Chmod) instead of the intended target, leaves the saved file behind, and never checks its contents.

TestSaveUploadedFileWithPermissionFailed depends on the environment: it expects an error from a 0o644 directory, which doesn't occur when running as root (e.g. in CI containers), and it can leave a "test" directory behind.
